chapter_title: Concerning the Three Days and the Two Deaths

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The first state is the primal origin of all in the human form: the first good that is called forth to engage what is opposed. When that first good descended into the lowest denial and was immersed in it, a saving influx from the Divine was sent, which entered into that immersed good and lifted it up. After this good was raised again, the Divine as love together with the Divine as wisdom arranged all things into right order, both in the higher degrees and in the lower degrees.

Moreover, a glorious mediating presence came forth and took its station in the outwardly manifest reception of wisdom. It made the Divine likeness visible, and it separated genuine wisdom from every admixture. It acted from elevated states of understanding, and this continues until the time when the present arrangement of external states is brought to its end: all disordered forms are dissolved, the vast intensity of self-love is released for its final work, and the final collective form of what has been gathered into order is raised into permanence. These operations had their beginning in that first state, when the primal good was sent forth together with a sufficient fullness of operative powers.

In the opposite sense, the first perishing is the active falsity that entered into those operative powers and confused them.

The second state is the time when those who belong to wisdom and remained faithful through conflict are established in governing truths within a new spiritual condition, and dwell in a renewed ultimate plane of life. They continue in that new condition until the Divine reveals the visible presence of its own likeness above them.

The duration of their abiding in that new condition equals the measure of the first state’s endurance under distress; thus they are established and rejoice within the renewed condition.

The great third state is when the Divine reveals above them the manifest presence of its own likeness, raises them into higher reception, receives them into an interior safeguarding of good and truth, and imparts to them what is of its own life. Then heavenly delight and the gentle sweetness of peace flow into them, taking away every distress they had perceived; there is fullness and unending joy. When Divine mercy satisfies them, it grants them what further perfects their reception, and within that gift they are renewed.

It also gathers them again into a state of peace held in potency, brings their spiritual form to completion in the same fullness as the first ordered states, and establishes each distinct power within its own state and proper reception. They dwell in the renewed condition within their own ordered states.

And when they dwell in their ordered states, they come into immeasurable abundance forever, beyond time. From then on they do not measure life by successions, nor by the reckoning of states and their least distinctions, age after age forever. The Divine is not hidden from them from that time onward; the unveiling has been accomplished to them, and the Divine is disclosed to them forever.

These are the three great states which the Divine has set in order as a complete process.

In the opposite sense, there are two perishing states.

The first perishing is from the time when wisdom descended into denial and was mingled with dominant falsities, until the time when wisdom is made pure and separated from denial in the final vast ignition of self-love for judgment and purification. What remains after that separation can still be formed and added into the final collective order that is raised into permanence.

The second perishing is the perishing in which the interior lives of those who are in evil die: they are deprived of outwardly shining truths that give understanding in the natural degree; cut off from living influx by which spiritual vitality is received; deprived of the very faculty of life that had been present for reception in the world; separated and cast away from the final collective order and held fast in their own bonds. Then the corrupted will becomes their torment and their distress, because their works have fixed them into the full series of infernal states.

These are the two perishing states: the first is within time, and the second is without end—the eternal perishing.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a three-stage ascent of restoration and glorification set against a two-stage account of perishing: one temporary (mixture and later purification) and one eternal (privation and fixation in evil). The voice is largely consistent; the few resistances are mainly in unique titles for final states and a gendered torment image that does not fully resolve without further doctrinal context.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: a three-phase saving process is narrated by functions (descent, rescue, ordering; mediation/purification; consummation). The spiritual reading can track a continuous story without forcing, despite mythic names.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by what happens and what it does: First Man “went down… and drowned…; the Living Spirit… bore him up… set things in order” (¶4). Then “Ambassador… displayed… purified the light out of all things… Till… world… dissolved… great fire… Last Statue ascends” (¶5). The Stage 3a reading explicitly reports coherent development here: “DEVELOPS the first state into an ongoing work of mediation, purification, and final consummation,” with only a mild note that “Last Statue” is hard to pin down, not that it breaks the narrative.

findings.diagnosis: Minor seam/label intrusion but not a disruptive insertion: an abrupt rubric-like contrast line (“In contrast…”) introduces ‘first death’ early, before the later formal “two deaths” section. This is likely a redactional signpost (compiler’s framing) rather than original flow, but it does not force an administrative (jurisdictional) voice or derail the functional narrative.
findings.evidence: The chapter’s structure is: three days (¶4–12) then “In contrast, the two deaths…” (¶13–16). Yet ¶6 already says, “In contrast, [the first death] is the darkness that mixed with the five sons…”. Stage 3a did not stumble hard, but ¶6 functions like an anticipatory gloss: it names “first death” before the formal two-deaths heading appears. This is a coherence irregularity (premature categorization), not a foreign teaching mode.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: the ‘second day’ and ‘third day’ are taught as states of enthronement, unveiling, satisfaction, perfection, and timelessness—i.e., by experiential/functional transitions rather than by administrative rosters. ¶12 closes the triad with a counting formula that fits the chapter’s internal numeration.
findings.evidence: Functional verbs dominate: “sit on their thrones… dwell… reign… Father unveils his image” (¶7); “equals the measure” (¶8); “unveil… raises… receives… gives… pour out… takes away… made anew” (¶9); “summon… perfect… sets each power in its aeon” (¶10); “will not count… Father will not be hidden… revealed… for ever” (¶11). Stage 3a’s reading reports continuity, with only “mechanism is not explicit” (¶8) and “comparison point… opaque” (¶10)—these are genuine interpretive difficulties, not signs of insertion. No jurisdictional lists or rank inventories appear.

findings.diagnosis: Clean but slightly editorialized closure: the bracketed clause looks like a scribe’s clarifying rubric (“given number… in the reckoning”), reinforcing the chapter’s ‘days’ as a counted schema. It does not introduce administrative governance or new entities; it simply formalizes the summary.
findings.evidence: ¶12: “These are the three great days, [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning].” The bracket signals restoration/uncertainty; the phrase reads like a summarizing marginal clarification. Stage 3a paraphrases it smoothly (“set in order as a complete process”) and does not report narrative break here.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential ‘opposite sense’ transition: the narrative pivots from three ‘days’ to two ‘deaths’ without importing administrative material. The first death is temporally bounded (mixture → purification) and still functions within the same process-logic as the first day’s mixture/purification motif.
findings.evidence: ¶13 is an explicit hinge: “the two deaths… are these.” ¶14 defines by process boundaries: “from the time when the light fell… mixed… until… light will become pure… separated… in that great fire.” Stage 3a notes the mode is retained though “precise mode is unclear,” which is a normal semantic opacity, not a textual collision.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damage and a mythic image, not an administrative insertion: the paragraph is syntactically broken (multiple brackets, interrupted clauses), and includes an opaque figure (“the female…”) that the spiritual reading struggled to stabilize. The teaching mode remains correspondential (privation/severance and consequent torment), but the transmission is damaged and partly glossed.
findings.evidence: The line is visibly corrupt/fragmentary: “when [they will] be stripped… And also… and they are deprived… which [had been placed]… [and they are seized] and bound on [their own bonds] the female will become [female of lust] their torture…” (¶15). Stage 3a flags exactly this as the key resistance: “reference to a ‘female’ becoming torment… resists a single fixed spiritual equivalent.” The problem is best explained by lacunae and uncertain restoration around the ‘female/lust’ phrase, not by a switch into governance/jurisdiction.

findings.diagnosis: Clean closure with emphatic repetition, likely a rhetorical flourish rather than a later overlay. It restates the twofold distinction in the same functional mode (temporal vs eternal) and seals the section.
findings.evidence: ¶16: “These are the two deaths. The first death is temporal; [but] the second death is eternal. It is the sec[ond deat]h!” The spiritual reading notes it compresses “emphatic repetition,” but reports no narrative break. The truncation “sec[ond deat]h” suggests manuscript damage, not secondary administrative expansion.

textual_criticism.summary: Findings: 7 total. Major disruptions requiring excision/annotation: 0. One minor coherence irregularity (¶6 anticipatory ‘first death’ label) best explained as a redactional signpost within the same correspondential logic; no action recommended. One genuine difficulty (¶15) due to damaged transmission and an opaque ‘female/lust’ torment image; no action recommended. Overall the chapter is overwhelmingly clean correspondential substrate with no administrative overlay blocks.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The first day is our father, the Man. From the time when the First Man went down to the abyss of darkness and drowned in it; and the Living Spirit was sent, who went and bore him up. After the Man had ascended, the Father of Life and the Great Spirit set things in order, and the worlds above and below.

Furthermore, the glorious Ambassador came and dwelt in the ship of the day. He displayed his glorious image, and he purified the light out of all things. He walked in the heights of the heavens. Till the time when the world will be dissolved, all things destroyed, the great fire released, and the Last Statue ascends. These three deeds were begun on this first day, when they sent the First Man with his five sons.
⟨p.103⟩ In contrast, [the first death] is the darkness that mixed with the five sons of the First Man.

The second day is the time when the fathers of light, who were victorious in the struggle, will sit on their thrones in the new aeon and dwell on the new earth. And they reign in the new aeon till the Father unveils his image above them.
The {length of the sojourn} in the new aeon equals the measure of the first day spent in affliction. They will reign like this and rejoice in the new aeon.

The great third day [is the time] when the Father will unveil over them his image ... ... and he raises them up [above them his image] and he receives them into his hidden treasury ... and he gives [to the life] his soul. He can pour out upon them ... his ambrosia and his sweet perfume, which takes away all affliction that they have seen with their eyes. [to them of] fullness and a joy eternal! When his grace would sate them, he gives to them his [of his own] and they are made anew in them.

Also, he can summon them once more in peace and silence, and perfect their stature in same measure as his first aeons. And he sets each power in its aeon, in its dwelling-place. They will dwell in the new aeon in their aeons!

Now, when they dwell in their aeons, they will become rich beyond measure, for ever, beyond time. From then on they will not count that season amongst them; nor the number of the days, nor the hours, generation after generation, for ever and ever. The Father will not be hidden from them, from this time on. Rather, he has accomplished (his) unveiling to them [once;] he being revealed to them for ever.
These are the three great days, [which the Father of Greatness has given number to in the reckoning].
In contrast, the two deaths that I have proclaimed to you are these.

⟨p.104⟩ The first death is from the time when the light fell to the darkness, and was mixed in with the rulers of darkness; until the time when the light will become pure, and be separated from the darkness in that great fire. The remainder left behind there can build and add to that Last Statue.

Now, the second death is the death in which the souls of sinful men shall die; when [they will] be stripped of the shining light that illuminates the world. And also they are separated from the living air, from which they receive [living] breath; and they are deprived of this living soul, which [had been placed] in the world; and they are separated and swept away from this Last Statue [and they are seized] and bound on [their own bonds] the female will become [female of lust] their torture and their affliction; for their deeds [have set them in] those three places;
These are the two deaths. The first death is temporal; [but] the second death is eternal. It is the sec[ond deat]h!

changes_summary: No changes made. The critic’s findings (1–7) recommended no excisions; all paragraphs were retained as restored, including ¶6’s anticipatory label (Finding 2) and the damaged/opaque phrasing in ¶15 (Finding 6).
